actions.action: Recut each cutting back to firm green tissue with sterilized blade
Check each cutting has a node
Let cut ends dry/callus before returning to water
Remove moss and use fresh water
Change water every 2-3 days and rinse the jug
Add cinnamon or a little hydrogen peroxide to water
Place cuttings in warm, bright, indirect light
Unpot parent plant and inspect roots and base
Trim black, mushy or smelly roots if present
Repot parent in fresh chunky aroid mix
Water parent only when top few inches are dry
Start over with new healthy stem sections if rot spreads
Post close-up photos of node area and parent base/roots

reason: The answer diagnoses rot rather than slow rooting. Its advice to remove the moss and be patient overlaps the fix, but it is buried among other steps. It also tells the owner to change the water every 2-3 days, the opposite of the fix, and to unpot a healthy parent plant, which is likely to delay rooting.
